title: stream-chunk-manifest-protocol-for-fragmented-json-and-escape-boundaries
creator: Lena Patel
description: Implement a robust, backward-compatible protocol to handle streaming structured JSON edge cases where escape sequences, unicode surrogate pairs, or partial tokens are split across chunks. The goal is to avoid silent corruption, enable safe client-side resume, and provide a graceful downgrade path (NDJSON/line-delimited) when strict reconstruction is impossible.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a small manifest frame at stream start describing framing mode and checkpoint granularity
Clients can request resume from a stable checkpoint token and receive a short patch sequence to reconcile partial tokens
Edge-case tests for: split escape sequences (\uXXXX across chunks), multi-byte UTF-8 crossing chunk boundary, and nested JSON strings with escaped quotes pass
When reconstruction is impossible (stream truncated mid-codepoint), server signals downgrade mode and provides NDJSON fallback without silent data loss
New mechanism is backwards-compatible: existing clients ignore the manifest and continue to receive regular chunked text
Documentation and SDK samples added for JS/Python demonstrating resume handshake and patch application
implementation_plan: Spike: validate corner cases using fuzzed chunkers against VMs and real models (2d)
Design: manifest frame spec + checkpoint token shape + patch format (1d)
Runtime: implement manifest emission and checkpoint recording (3d)
Client SDK: resume/patch handlers in JS and Python (2d)
E2E tests: streaming harness with artificial truncation/resume scenarios (2d)
Docs and migration guide, plus example PRs for sample apps (1d)
design_notes: We introduce a non-intrusive 'manifest' control frame at t=0. It is a short JSON object prefixed with a control marker '<<MANIFEST>>' to avoid protocol confusion.
Manifest contains: framing_mode ("chunked"), checkpoint_interval (bytes), checkpoint_id_seed (base64), fallback_mode ('ndjson'|'none')
Checkpoint tokens are opaque base64 strings derived from a monotonic stream position + hash of last complete UTF-8 codepoint boundary to ensure idempotent resumes
Patch format mirrors a minimal NDJSON patch stream: ordered atomic operations that replace/insert text ranges. We keep it text-first to avoid binary transport changes
We favour replayable patches over naive byte offsets to accommodate lossy intermediaries (proxies) that may alter chunk boundaries
tradeoffs: Pros: deterministic resume with small manifest, graceful fallback, backward-compatible for old clients
Cons: small initial metadata overhead and slightly more server bookkeeping for checkpoints
Alternative considered: always emit strict chunk-aligned JSON frames (too disruptive to existing SDKs and high overhead)
qa_steps: Run fuzz harness with 1M randomized chunks validating decoder invariants
Create targeted scenarios: surrogate pair split, multi-byte UTF-8 split, escaped-slash across chunks
Simulate client retry with dropped last N bytes and assert patch application yields identical JSON tree
Test fallback: forcibly truncate stream within a codepoint and ensure fallback NDJSON is produced and consumed by SDK sample
Measure percent increase in tail-latency due to checkpoint writes and ensure <3% impact under 99th percentile for small requests
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest encoder/decoder, integration tests in streaming harness, and SDK acceptance tests in smoke suite. Add CI job that runs fuzz harness nightly and fails build on regressions.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Lena Patel: Triage - high frequency support requests for broken JSON after transient network hiccups. Spike requested to assess feasibility of client-resumable streams.

2026-02-18 - Marco Chen: Spike completed - fuzzed chunker found consistent failure modes when '\u' escapes and multi-byte UTF-8 sequences are split. Proposed manifest+patch approach. Initial perf penalty is small.

2026-02-22 - Design review (Sofia Andersson): reviewed manifest draft. Ask to reduce manifest size and ensure it degrades if proxies strip control markers. Decided to prefix with '<<MANIFEST>>' and include a short magic version.
2026-03-02 - PR opened: runtime changes to emit manifest and checkpoint hooks. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891
2026-03-05 - Code review (Ben Torres): request to add stronger checksum on checkpoint token to detect mid-checkpoint truncation. Marco to add CRC32+sha1 slice.
2026-03-10 - QA: initial harness passes happy paths, uncovered a bug where patch reordering could happen under concurrent resume. Locking added to patch queue to maintain order.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: In Progress - SDK patches in review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/1042). Planning to merge runtime changes behind feature flag 'manifest_v1' to limit blast radius. Targeting release runtime-1.22
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: middleboxes may remove control markers -> Mitigation: manifest is optional and server will detect missing manifest by absence of handshake response; in this case we fall back to conservative NDJSON mode
Risk: increased metadata overhead for micro requests -> Mitigation: manifest is only emitted for streaming responses and can be disabled per-route via config
Risk: clients with older SDKs may misinterpret patch frames -> Mitigation: patches are sent only on explicit resume requests initiated by client; existing normal flows unaffected
release_notes_snippet: Streaming: added optional manifest + resume patch protocol to improve resilience for streaming structured JSON (escape/codepoint boundary handling). SDKs updated to support handshake and safe resume. Disabled by default; enabled per-route or via feature flag.
followups: ENG-45012 - telemetry for resumptions and patch success rate
ENG-45501 - SDK ergonomic improvements for patch appliers
